subject: Science
stem: Before a science lesson, a teacher writes the specific learning objective on the board: 'Students will be able to state the three states of matter and give one example of each.' This clear, measurable statement of what students should achieve is called a/an:
explanation: Instructional objectives are specific, observable, measurable statements of what learners should be able to do by the end of a lesson — guiding both teaching activities and later assessment.

subject: Science
stem: A science teacher wants to assess not just whether students remember facts, but whether they can apply scientific concepts to solve a novel, real-world problem. This requires designing questions at which level(s) of Bloom's revised taxonomy?

options.option_text: Apply and Analyse (or higher), not just Remember
None of Bloom's levels are relevant to science

explanation: Applying scientific concepts to novel situations requires questions at the Apply/Analyse level (or higher) of Bloom's revised taxonomy, not just Remember-level recall of facts.
